v1.feedback: The collapse-wave sweeping top→bottom and the iridescence→violet-grey palette shift are genuine elegy gestures that clearly descend from the soap-bubble parent — this isn't a rename. However, the 18s cycle repeating the same collapse undermines the finality an elegy needs; consider making the collapse irreversible or progressively deeper each cycle so the form truly erodes. The tube base radius (0.40) is thin enough that the structure may read wispy rather than monumental — thickening the rings, especially pre-collapse, would give the decay more visual weight to lose. A subtle camera drift inward as the form crumbles would reinforce the intimacy of watching something fade.

v2.feedback: The elegy concept genuinely drives the design — thin-film iridescence draining to violet-grey ash, the downward erosion wave wilting the tube, and the global opacity fade all read as mourning rather than decoration. Two risks: the progressive fade-to-background (`globalFade = uDecay * 0.25` plus per-ring alpha collapse) may erase too much of the form late-stage, leaving a near-empty canvas — clamp minimum alpha around 0.15 so the skeletal remains stay visible as a memorial silhouette. Second, the erosion wave sweeps uniformly; introducing slight per-ring stochastic delay (seeded from ring height) would make the collapse feel more organic and less like a screen wipe.
